primary_diagnosis: Chronic kidney disease from nephrotoxic/substance exposure
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient’s chronic substance‑use disorder provides the strongest link to his stage 3 CKD, outweighing other considerations. Concurrent uncontrolled epilepsy with frequent analgesic use adds a second major contributor to renal stress. Hematologic abnormalities (elevated PDW) raise concern for an early myeloproliferative disorder. Secondary hypertension, tubular acidosis, and other endocrine possibilities are retained but carry lower confidence due to limited supporting data. The differential reflects the reviewer’s probability adjustments and removes diagnoses deemed unsupported.
unresolved_findings: Markedly elevated platelet distribution width (PDW 189.6 fL) without clear cause
Borderline low fasting glucose (69.8 mg/dL) with downward trend
Mild non‑anion‑gap metabolic acidosis (CO₂ total 20.4 mmol/L)
Missing BMI, eGFR, lipid‑panel summary, smoking status, family history, urinalysis, and neuroimaging
recommended_workup: Comprehensive urinalysis with protein quantification and microscopy
Serum aldosterone/renin ratio to evaluate primary aldosteronism
Polysomnography to assess for obstructive sleep apnea
Thyroid panel (TSH, free T4) and cortisol level
CBC with peripheral smear and possibly bone marrow biopsy for thrombocythemia
Serum electrolytes, arterial blood gas, urine electrolytes to confirm RTA
Fasting cortisol and ACTH stimulation test to investigate low glucose
Toxicology screen for nephrotoxic agents (e.g., NSAIDs, illicit drugs)
Medication reconciliation focusing on nephrotoxic and seizure‑related drugs
Assessment of glycemic status (HbA1c, repeat fasting glucose)
Lipid panel and cardiovascular risk assessment
